summary: Describes a way for application servers to locate and use media servers in SIP networks. Media servers provide basic building blocks such as announcements, user interaction, and conferencing. The memo defines an interoperable interface so those building blocks can be combined into larger applications. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4240 explains how a SIP application can request a basic media service from a media server. The service name and its settings go in the SIP address, so the request uses existing SIP messages.

subtitle: A SIP convention for asking a media server to play announcements, run voice dialogs, or mix a conference.

tldr.problem: SIP applications need a consistent way to find and request basic media services from different media servers.
tldr.mechanism: The request names a service in the SIP URI user part and supplies service parameters in the URI. The client sends a SIP INVITE; SIP itself is unchanged.
tldr.outcome: The memo describes interoperable interfaces for announcements, prompt-and-collect dialogs, and basic conference mixing. It does not cover enhanced conference controls.

today: RFC 4240 is Informational and was published in December 2005. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Basic Services, One Request Method
sections.content:
SIP networks use media servers for three basic tasks: playing announcements, collecting a user's response to a prompt, and mixing media for a conference. RFC 4240 defines a shared way for an application server to locate and invoke these services.

The method does not change SIP or the meaning of a SIP Request-URI. Devices that do not implement the convention are not required to change their behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo defines a consistent way for an application to request three basic media services. It leaves SIP itself unchanged.

sections.title: Naming a Service in a SIP Address
sections.content:
A media server reads the service indicator from the user part of the SIP Request-URI. The indicator contains a service name and may include an instance identifier separated by an equal sign. URI parameters carry additional settings. The service indicator is case-insensitive.

If the server cannot perform or recognize a requested service, it returns 488 NOT ACCEPTABLE HERE. If the service requires an existing instance and that instance is absent, it returns 404 NOT FOUND.
sections.plainLanguage: The part of the SIP address before the at sign names the service. Parameters after the address provide settings, such as which announcement to play.

sections.title: Announcements, Dialogs, and Conferences
sections.content:
The announcement service uses annc; its required play parameter identifies the resource or provisioned sequence. Other parameters can set repetition, delay, duration, locale, or substitution values. The server may play one multimedia object with multiple streams, but not multiple objects in the same dialog.

The prompt-and-collect service uses dialog with a voicexml script URI. The conference service uses conf=identifier: an INVITE creates a session if one does not exist and resources are available, or joins an existing session. A BYE removes a dialog leg; the session remains while at least one dialog is associated with it.
sections.plainLanguage: An announcement request names what to play, while a dialog request points to a VoiceXML script. A conference request uses one identifier so participants can join the same mixing session.

sections.title: Security and Service Limits
sections.content:
The media server should authenticate and authorize endpoints according to local policy. It must implement the sips: scheme because some interactions carry confidential or integrity-sensitive information. The RFC recommends using the server's security services where appropriate.

An announcement set to repeat forever can consume resources. The RFC recommends local limits or other controls. It also notes a billing concern with early-media announcements and says this is one reason that service is deprecated.
sections.plainLanguage: The server should check who may use its services and protect sensitive exchanges. It should also limit requests that could keep a service running indefinitely.
